note: Generated from each plugins/<name>/profile.ttl. Do not edit; run npm run build:index.

plugins.label: 8-Bit 8asterd
plugins.comment: Three AY-3-8910 chips under the 8b8 firmware, running unmodified as WebAssembly. Nine voices across three chips, hardware envelopes, a percussion set on channel 10, and the firmware's own vibrato, tremolo, arpeggiator, buzzy bass, circuit bending and ten tuning temperaments.
cautions: Nine voices across three chips, and the tenth note steals the oldest rather than being refused. Percussion and pitched notes come out of the same nine.
Percussion is MIDI channel 10, notes 35 to 59. Pitched notes are 24 to 96 on any other channel, and anything outside that is ignored rather than transposed into range.

Every control answers to a MIDI CC as well, one controller per port as the profile's midi:binding declarations say, which is what the hardware does. A host automating a parameter and a controller sending its CC will fight.
Roll and Retrigger are positions on an exponential curve from about 1.5Hz to 45Hz rather than a rate in hertz. The figure shown is the one the device's own panel shows.
The firmware's EEPROM is a scratch array that is never persisted. Its SAVE command has nowhere to write, and settings belong in the project graph instead.

plugins.label: BassGen
plugins.comment: Transport synced bass line generator. Scale, genre and subdivision shape a seeded pattern that plays in time with the session and can be steered from a keyboard.
cautions: Silent until the host transport is rolling and reports a tempo and a beat position. A generator with no idea what time it is would be guessing, and this one says so by producing nothing.
Monophonic by design. A new step ends the note before it rather than overlapping.

plugins.label: Boost
plugins.comment: A gain stage in C++, the minimal starting point for a WebAssembly Jig: everything in boost.cpp beyond jig_process is ABI wiring, meant to be copied.

plugins.label: Cadence
plugins.comment: Transport synced MIDI harmonizer that learns a chord cycle from what it hears and plays voiced progressions with comping in time with the session.
cautions: Silent until it has learned a cycle: play notes into it while the transport rolls, and it starts harmonizing at the next cycle boundary.
Pure MIDI, no audio: route its MIDI output to an instrument. Learn is a trigger that fires on the rising edge.
With pass_input on, incoming notes continue downstream alongside the harmony.

plugins.label: Canticle
plugins.comment: Twelve-voice polyphonic tonal instrument for the middle of an ensemble: keys, reed, pad, pluck and glass tones for melody, counterpoint and chords.
cautions: Twelve voices. A thirteenth note steals the oldest, releasing voices first, rather than being refused.
A velocity-100 single note reaches at least -10 dBFS at the default setting on every model; dense chords stay bounded through the final soft clip.
CC 120 and 123 silence every voice, like an all-notes-off.

plugins.label: Cascade
plugins.comment: Schroeder plate reverb with per-mode scaling, damping inside the feedback loop, and a freeze that holds the tail indefinitely.
cautions: Freeze holds the tail at unity feedback. Following it with a limiter is wise when several instances are frozen at once.

plugins.label: Conductor
plugins.comment: Cuts the transport into bar-aligned sections (intro, development, break, reprise, coda), as an editable form of up to 12 steps or by seeded weighted choice, and at each boundary sends a section note and CCs for scene, density, energy, mutation and reset to whatever listens on its channel. Each section can have its own length limits and its own scene, density, energy and mutation values, and may restart the generators listening to it.
cautions: Silent until the host transport is rolling and reports a tempo and a beat position. Pure MIDI, no audio: route its MIDI output to the plugins that should follow it, and set their Conductor channel to this plugin's MIDI channel (16 by default). Ported from the Downspout VST3 of the same name; its panel and status read-outs are not carried over, and the random draw is the VST3's 64-bit mix.
Declares no jig:module and so no jig:abi. A host that loads a module directly, such as the native adapter, cannot load this plugin; a JavaScript AudioWorklet host can.

plugins.label: Counterpointer
plugins.comment: Transport synced MIDI processor that learns an incoming cycle and answers it with a monophonic counter-melody, in counterpoint or a descending bass register.
cautions: Silent until the transport rolls and a full cycle of incoming MIDI has been captured. A counter-melody with nothing to answer would be guessing, and this one says so by producing nothing.
Pure MIDI, no audio: route its MIDI output to an instrument. Learn is a trigger that fires on the rising edge, so each press is one action.
Monophonic by design. A new step ends the note before it rather than overlapping.
With pass_input on, incoming notes continue downstream alongside the counter-melody, including while stopped or still learning.

plugins.label: Dice
plugins.comment: A MIDI probability gate: each note-on passes with the set probability, and a note-off passes if and only if its note-on did. The generator's evolving state is saved with the project, so a restored session gates exactly as the saved one would have.
cautions: Declares no jig:module and so no jig:abi. A host that loads a module directly, such as the native adapter, cannot load this plugin; a JavaScript AudioWorklet host can.
A dropped note-on also drops its note-off, so nothing downstream is left sustaining. Anything that is not a note passes through untouched.

plugins.label: DrumGen
plugins.comment: Transport synced MIDI drum generator. Genre, style mode and resolution shape a seeded pattern that plays in time with the session, with fills on the last bar of the loop and Conductor CC control.
cautions: Silent until the host transport is rolling and reports a tempo and a beat position. A generator with no idea what time it is would be guessing, and this one says so by producing nothing.
Pure MIDI, no audio: route its MIDI output to a drum instrument. New, Mutate and Fill are triggers that fire on the rising edge, so each press is one action.
A held note with no note off is a stuck note, so stopping the transport sounds the ringing notes now rather than leaving them held.

plugins.label: DrumKit
plugins.comment: Eleven voice synthesised drum instrument. MIDI notes trigger the voices, the master bus adds crush, drive and room, and per-instrument mutes cut voices immediately.
cautions: One-shot voices: note-offs do nothing, and a hit cannot be choked except the open hat, which a closed hat cuts short.
CC 120 and 123 reset every voice and the master bus, like an all-notes-off.
The eleven trig outputs the native wrapper exposes as UI LEDs are not parameters here and have no panel control.

plugins.label: Dynamix
plugins.comment: Compressor/expander, limiter and clipper/soft distortion in series. A second stereo input on channels 3 and 4 is an external key: when it is connected, the compressor/expander stage reads its level from that instead of the main signal, for sidechain ducking. When nothing is connected there, the stage detects on the main signal itself.
cautions: The limiter has no lookahead: it reacts within a fraction of a millisecond rather than before the transient, so a very sharp attack can still touch the ceiling briefly before the gain catches up. Leave a little headroom below the ceiling for material with hard transients.

The compressor/expander stage links its gain reduction across both channels from a single detected level, so it never shifts the stereo image, but it also means the side chain input's balance between its own two channels, not just its overall level, feeds the detector.
Disconnecting the side chain input mid-session returns the compressor/expander to detecting on the main signal on the next block, not instantly at the sample the cable was pulled.

plugins.label: Ferrite
plugins.comment: A neural amp model (nam-rs, MIT, ported from and validated against the reference Python and C++ implementations) in series with an impulse response, a cabinet or a room of up to 2.7 seconds, by partitioned FFT convolution. The amp can be switched off to use it as a convolution reverb, and Mix blends the convolved signal with the dry one. Ships a small example .nam and a synthetic (not captured) cabinet IR; both jig:asset resources are meant to be replaced with your own.
cautions: The neural model and the cabinet impulse response are both loaded at the sample rate they were captured or trained at, 48 kHz for the example model here. This plugin does not resample: a host running at a different rate gets a load that reports a mismatch (see the module's own jig_load_nam and jig_load_ir return codes) rather than silently wrong output.
The shipped impulse response is synthetic, generated for this example, not a real cabinet capture.
One amp model, run on the mean of both input channels: an amp is a mono device, and a real capture is too heavy to run twice.
Impulse responses are normalised to unit energy, so a response sets the tone and not the level. Stereo responses are mixed to mono.
Needs WebAssembly SIMD, which every current browser has. The native adapter's interpreter does not, and could not run a real capture in real time if it did.

Light runs the smallest network of a slimmable .nam, about a seventh of the work and a little less detailed, for a phone or a busy session. A .nam that is not slimmable has one network and ignores it.

plugins.label: Ground
plugins.comment: Transport synced long-form bass generator. Form shapes and phrase roles plan a whole section that plays in time with the session, with arc tension and Conductor control including scene-driven role overrides.
cautions: Silent until the host transport is rolling and reports a tempo and a beat position. A generator with no idea what time it is would be guessing, and this one says so by producing nothing.
Pure MIDI, no audio: route its MIDI output to a bass instrument. New Form, New Phrase and Mutate Cell are triggers that fire on the rising edge, so each press is one action.
Monophonic by design. A new note ends the note before it rather than overlapping.

plugins.label: JigDAW Gain Trim
plugins.comment: Converted by bin/jsfx-import.js from examples/jsfx/gain-trim.jsfx, a REAPER JSFX effect, and run under the shared interpreter in plugins/_jsfx-runtime/.
cautions: Converted from JSFX by a restricted EEL2 subset: no user-defined function, no strings, no gmem, and while()/loop() are bounded so a runaway script goes silent rather than missing the audio thread's deadline. See plugins/_jsfx-runtime/README.md.

plugins.label: JigDAW One-Pole Filter
plugins.comment: Converted by bin/jsfx-import.js from examples/jsfx/one-pole-filter.jsfx, a REAPER JSFX effect, and run under the shared interpreter in plugins/_jsfx-runtime/.
cautions: Converted from JSFX by a restricted EEL2 subset: no user-defined function, no strings, no gmem, and while()/loop() are bounded so a runaway script goes silent rather than missing the audio thread's deadline. See plugins/_jsfx-runtime/README.md.

plugins.label: JigDAW Soft Clipper
plugins.comment: Converted by bin/jsfx-import.js from examples/jsfx/soft-clipper.jsfx, a REAPER JSFX effect, and run under the shared interpreter in plugins/_jsfx-runtime/.
cautions: Converted from JSFX by a restricted EEL2 subset: no user-defined function, no strings, no gmem, and while()/loop() are bounded so a runaway script goes silent rather than missing the audio thread's deadline. See plugins/_jsfx-runtime/README.md.

plugins.label: Keyframe
plugins.comment: Stretches audio in time and shifts its pitch, independently, by reducing the signal to its local extrema and crossfading between playheads over a span the extrema's own density chooses.
cautions: The algorithm is Matthew Nielsen's, Keyframe Time Stretching via Extrema Sampling, DAFx26, CC BY 4.0. This implementation is written from the paper.
It colours the sound: added saturation and some blurring of spectral detail. It is at its best on dense, layered material and percussion, and at its weakest on solo voice and bells.

A live input cannot be played faster than it arrives, so a time rate above 100 percent plays at the input's own rate, and with a pitch shift it splices back repeatedly. Below 100 percent the output falls behind the input by up to eight seconds and then skips forward. Both skips are splices, and both are audible.
Economy quality joins the extrema with straight lines, which is the roughest reconstruction. Balanced and Full use a smooth curve between them. Full also places each extremum between samples.
Changing Quality or Stereo empties the capture and restarts it, so it is heard as a short gap.
Latency is a fixed 512 frames, which is two forced keyframe hops.

plugins.label: Lookahead
plugins.comment: A switchable lookahead delay for time-aligning parallel paths: direct, or held back by 512 frames. Changing position changes the plugin's latency, which the host compensates.
cautions: Declares no jig:module and so no jig:abi. A host that loads a module directly, such as the native adapter, cannot load this plugin; a JavaScript AudioWorklet host can.

Changing position changes latency while audio flows. The host recompensates from the reported frame, and the switch itself is audible as a jump: latency.md says a plugin that can pad to its worst case should, and this one exists to exercise the other path.

plugins.label: Markov
plugins.comment: Markov-chain melody generator: a random walk over the twelve pitch classes driven by a 12 by 12 transition matrix, filled by one of eight styles or learned from a melodic line on its MIDI input, and played in time with the host transport.
cautions: Silent until the host transport is rolling and reports a tempo and a beat position. Pure MIDI, no audio: route its MIDI output to an instrument. Ported from the Downspout VST3 of the same name; the status read-outs and the panel are not carried over, and the random draw is the VST3's 64-bit mix.

The matrix is set by Style and Randomise, or learned. The VST3's cell-by-cell matrix editor is not carried over. The matrix and what it has learned are the plugin's saved state, so a reopened session plays the same melody.
Declares no jig:module and so no jig:abi. A host that loads a module directly, such as the native adapter, cannot load this plugin; a JavaScript AudioWorklet host can.

plugins.label: MelGen
plugins.comment: Transport synced phrase-aware melody generator. Period, contour and answer shape a seeded line that plays in time with the session, follows an incoming line when asked, and answers Conductor CCs.
cautions: Silent until the host transport is rolling and reports a tempo and a beat position. A generator with no idea what time it is would be guessing, and this one says so by producing nothing.
Pure MIDI, no audio: route its MIDI output to an instrument. New, Notes and Rhythm are triggers that fire on the rising edge, so each press is one action.
Monophonic by design. A new note ends the note before it rather than overlapping.

plugins.label: MIDI Filter
plugins.comment: Steers MIDI between plugins: keeps one channel or all, moves what it keeps to another channel, transposes notes, and passes only the notes inside a range, so two of them split a keyboard between two instruments. A note-off passes only for a note-on that passed, so nothing is left sustaining when a setting changes mid-note.
cautions: Declares no jig:module and so no jig:abi. A host that loads a module directly, such as the native adapter, cannot load this plugin; a JavaScript AudioWorklet host can.
Only the note range and transpose touch notes. Control changes, pitch bend and other channel messages follow the channel settings alone, and system messages always pass.

plugins.label: Moka
plugins.comment: A stereo MIDI synth built on modal synthesis: each voice is a bank of eight damped sine modes struck by a short mallet transient, giving xylophone, glockenspiel, woodblock, glass bowl, metal sheet and tube voices.
cautions: Follows per-channel pitch bend (2 semitones, or the range set by RPN 0), so Retune can drive it microtonally. Ported from the Downspout VST3 of the same name; its factory presets and panel are not carried over.
Declares no jig:module and so no jig:abi. A host that loads a module directly, such as the native adapter, cannot load this plugin; a JavaScript AudioWorklet host can.

plugins.label: Monochord
plugins.comment: Eight-voice waveguide string, plucked, bowed or hammered: a delay line closed into a tuned loop with damping, stiffness, a pickup comb and a small body.
cautions: A ninth note steals the quietest voice rather than being refused.
Exciter changes apply to the next note. A note already sounding keeps the exciter it started with.
The bow keeps sounding while the key is held and its level follows the note velocity; Hardness does not affect it.
Stiffness above about 0.7 detunes the upper partials audibly on a low note (partial 6 is +3 cents at 0.5, +20 at 0.7, +62 at 0.9).

plugins.label: Mop
plugins.comment: Eighteen voice OPL3 FM General MIDI instrument, capped at eight voices by default, based on mop by M. Glargaard. The AdLib Sound Blaster sound of DOS-era games: FM timbres from mop's own bank, a drum kit on channel 10, and every control answering to a MIDI CC.
cautions: Eight voices by default out of the eighteen the chip has. A ninth note steals the oldest voice rather than being refused; raise Voices toward eighteen for dense arrangements.
Percussion is MIDI channel 10, notes 35 to 81. Pitched notes play on any other channel.
The Program control sets the instrument on every melodic channel at once, which is how presets are auditioned. An incoming program change overrides a single channel without moving the panel.

Every control but Program answers to a MIDI CC as well, one controller per port as the profile's midi:binding declarations say. A host automating a parameter and a controller sending its CC will fight.
Channel volume, expression, pan, sustain and pitch bend arrive as MIDI on each channel and are not panel controls: CC 7, 11, 10 and 64 behave as mop does.

plugins.label: Octet
plugins.comment: Eight-band parametric equalizer, stereo, with 12 and 48 dB cuts, shelves, bells and notches, Left/Right and Mid/Side modes, a spectrum analyser and a graphic editor with a draggable node per band. A fresh instance passes the signal unchanged.
cautions: The graphic display (the response curves, a node to drag for each band and the spectrum analyser) is the plugin's own editor. A host shows it only for a plugin served from another origin than its own page; every control is also on the generated panel.
MIDI controllers 1 to 4 on the CC channel drive one band and the output, as in Drift. The panel does not follow them.
The 48 dB cuts are 8th-order Butterworth; a corner within a few percent of half the sample rate behaves like a gentler slope, because the bilinear transform compresses the top octave.

plugins.label: Parameq
plugins.comment: Six-band stereo parametric equalizer in C++: peak, low and high shelf, low and high pass, band pass and notch shapes per band, each with its own enable, frequency, gain and Q.
cautions: A low pass or high pass corner within a few percent of Nyquist (half the sample rate) behaves like a gentler slope than the shape suggests, because the bilinear transform compresses the top octave.

plugins.label: Pulse
plugins.comment: Eight voice subtractive synthesiser with saw, square and triangle oscillators, a one-pole lowpass and an attack-release envelope.
cautions: Eight voices. A ninth note steals the oldest voice rather than being refused.

plugins.label: Quartet
plugins.comment: Eight-voice four-operator FM synthesiser with eleven algorithms, band-limited sine, saw and square operators, per-operator envelopes, feedback, optional 2x oversampling, a pitch envelope and a multimode filter. It opens as a mono bass.
cautions: It opens as a bass: algorithm 1, mono, a 24 dB low-pass at 2.4 kHz. Set Play Mode to Poly for chords.
A ninth note steals the quietest voice rather than being refused.
The panel does not draw the routing or the filter response the VST3 does; the algorithm is named in its choice list instead.

plugins.label: Quefrency
plugins.comment: Separates its input through the cepstrum into a formant envelope and a harmonic structure, shifts and reshapes each independently, and multiplies them back together.
cautions: Latency is 2047 frames at 50 kHz and below, and 4095 above. The processor reports the figure for the actual rate; the module ABI carries no latency, so a native host is not told it and will not compensate.
The formant envelope of a chord is the envelope of the whole mixture. Pitch shift moves every spectral peak, so chords stay chords, but it cannot act on one note of a chord alone.
Transients smear when pitch or frequency shift is set, as with any phase vocoder.
Lifter must sit below the shortest pitch period in the input, or harmonics leak into the formant envelope and move with it.

MIDI control changes drive the parameters, one controller per port as the profile's midi:binding declarations say, on any channel. Value 64 is each parameter's default where the default lies inside its range, so a centred controller changes nothing; 64 and above selects the true envelope.
A controller's value is not shown on the panel and is not saved with the project. It holds until the host's own value for that parameter next changes, and then the host's value wins.

plugins.label: Retune
plugins.comment: Retunes a note stream to a Scala (.scl) scale by sending each held note on its own channel (2 to 16) behind a per-note pitch bend, so any synth that follows per-channel pitch bend can play microtonally.
cautions: The receiving synth must apply pitch bend per channel at the configured Bend range, in a one channel per note mode. Incoming pitch bend, channel aftertouch and system messages are dropped.

The scale is a jig:asset the person replaces with a .scl file of their own; it is saved with the session. Ported from the Downspout VST3 of the same name, whose .kbm keyboard maps and MPE zone setup are also not supported here.
Declares no jig:module and so no jig:abi. A host that loads a module directly, such as the native adapter, cannot load this plugin; a JavaScript AudioWorklet host can.

plugins.label: Sam
plugins.comment: Software Automatic Mouth, the 1982 Commodore 64 formant speech synthesiser, as an instrument: typed text is spoken either one word per MIDI note, sung at the pitch of the key, or one word per step from a start bar, locked to the host transport.
cautions: Transport mode is silent while the host is stopped (use Speak to audition) and when the host gives no beat position. Keys mode ignores the transport.

The words are a jig:asset the person replaces with a plain text file of their own, up to 2000 printable ASCII characters and 512 words, and are saved with the session. A lone _ is a rest. Phonetic reads SAM phoneme codes, e.g. /HEH3LOW2 WER4LD.

SAM's code is vendored in third_party/ and has no licence (abandonware; see third_party/SAM-LICENSE.md). Whether it may be redistributed with this plugin is the repository owner's decision, recorded in HUMANS.md.
Ported from the Downspout VST3 of the same name. Not carried over: the six voice presets (set Speed, Pitch, Throat and Mouth by hand) and the Current Word read-out.

plugins.label: Sprout
plugins.comment: L-system MIDI generator: a grammar is rewritten for up to 16 generations, read as a turtle, and played as a monophonic, scale-quantised line locked to the host transport, optionally growing by one generation every few bars.
cautions: Silent until the host transport is rolling and reports a tempo and a beat position. Pure MIDI, no audio: route its MIDI output to an instrument. Ported from the Downspout VST3 of the same name; the status read-outs and the panel are not carried over, and the random draw is the VST3's 64-bit mix.
Monophonic by design. A new note ends the note before it rather than overlapping. An expansion longer than 131,072 symbols is not used; the deepest generation that fits plays instead.
Declares no jig:module and so no jig:abi. A host that loads a module directly, such as the native adapter, cannot load this plugin; a JavaScript AudioWorklet host can.

plugins.label: Squelch
plugins.comment: A resonant lowpass filter whose cutoff an envelope follower pushes up on every note, for the acid bass sweep. Put it after a synth: each note opens the filter and Decay sets how fast it closes. Plain JavaScript, no WebAssembly module.
cautions: Resonance stops short of self-oscillation, and the output is soft clipped to keep a note on the resonant peak from being much louder than the rest.
Declares no jig:module and so no jig:abi. A host that loads a module directly, such as the native adapter, cannot load this plugin; a JavaScript AudioWorklet host can.

plugins.label: Stomp rack
plugins.comment: A boost into a tremolo into a plate reverb, as one plugin: Drive, Tremolo depth and Reverb mix are all it exposes. The rack is built from three published Jigs by reference, and is the worked example of a composite plugin.

plugins.label: Tremolo
plugins.comment: Amplitude modulation by a sine LFO. Its whole signal path is JavaScript: no WebAssembly module, the worked example for a plugin whose processing does not need one.
cautions: Declares no jig:module and so no jig:abi. A host that loads a module directly, such as the native adapter, cannot load this plugin; a JavaScript AudioWorklet host can.
